status: experimental assurance/finality architecture; no production promotion
purpose: Define provisional/finality states, challenge windows, evidence-retention floors, and transition rules so later review remains possible without retaining every byte forever.

challenge_window.rule: Each challengeable event declares who may challenge, opening time, closing time, escalation target, and evidence that must remain available until the window and any active appeal conclude.
challenge_window.default_effect: A challenge changes review/finality state; it does not itself authorize rollback, punishment, or compensation.

retention_invariants: evidence required for an open challenge or appeal cannot be deleted merely because an ordinary retention period elapsed
legal/policy hold must be explicit, scoped, reviewable, and separately authorized
retention can be minimized by replacing raw material with sufficient digests, receipts, redactions, or proofs only where reviewability is preserved
retention policy does not authorize disclosure
deletion policy does not authorize destruction of evidence subject to an active challenge, appeal, rollback dependency, or hold
finalization may reduce future retention obligations but never permits silent rewriting of historical records
expired challenge windows do not make a claim objectively true; they only change procedural state

allowed_only_if: effect is reversible or compensable under a separately validated profile
forbidden_for: irreversible effects lacking pre-execution required assurance
actions whose rollback path depends on unavailable external authority
effects whose challenge evidence would be destroyed by execution

nonclaims: This profile does not define legal limitation periods or court deadlines.
Finalized does not mean infallible or unchallengeable under every external process.
Retention classes do not determine lawful retention in any jurisdiction.
This profile does not promote optimistic execution as a current production capability.
